Title: Retrieve paginated list of customers for a shop with default pagination parameters
Preconditions: Shop with ID 1 has at least 15 customers recorded in the system
Steps: 1. Send a GET request to /api/customers/by-shop/1 with no query parameters (defaults: page=0, limit=10).
Expected Result: HTTP 200 OK response with a JSON body containing: {"status": "success", "message": "Customers retrieved successfully", "data": {"content": [<list of 10 customers>], "totalElements": 15, "totalPages": 2, "size": 10, "number": 0}}

Title: Verify that retrieving customers by shop ID enforces proper authorization (insecure direct object reference) - unauthorized user cannot access another shop's customer list
Preconditions: Two shops (Shop A and Shop B) exist with at least one customer each. User has valid authentication token for Shop A but no access to Shop B.
Steps:
1. Send a GET request to /api/customers/by-shop/{shopId} with shopId set to Shop B's ID, using the authenticated user's token. 2. Observe the response.

Test Data: shopId = [ID of Shop B]
Expected Result: The API responds with HTTP status 403 (Forbidden) or 404 (Not Found), and the response body contains a generic error message (e.g., 'Access denied' or 'Shop not found'). No customer data for Shop B is returned.

Title: Verify that retrieving customers by shop ID with a non-existent shop ID returns a generic error message without exposing system details
Preconditions: User has valid authentication token for any shop.
Steps:
1. Send a GET request to /api/customers/by-shop/{shopId} with shopId set to a non-existent ID (e.g., 999999). 2. Observe the response.

Test Data: shopId = 999999
Expected Result: The API responds with HTTP status 404 (Not Found) and a response body containing 'status: error', 'message: No customers found for this shop', and no sensitive system details (e.g., stack traces, database errors).

Title: Verify that retrieving customers by shop ID with malicious input (e.g., SQL injection, path traversal) is rejected
Preconditions: User has valid authentication token for any shop.
Steps:
1. Send a GET request to /api/customers/by-shop/{shopId} with shopId set to malicious input (e.g., '1 OR 1=1', '../../'). 2. Observe the response.

Test Data: shopId = '1 OR 1=1' (or '../../')
Expected Result: The API responds with HTTP status 400 (Bad Request) or 404 (Not Found) and a response body containing 'status: error', 'message: Invalid shop ID', and no sensitive system details.

Title: Verify that special instructions in order items are properly sanitized to prevent injection attacks (e.g., XSS, script tags)
Preconditions: User has valid authentication token for a shop and a customer exists.
Steps:
1. Send a POST request to /api/orders with a payload containing special instructions with malicious content (e.g., '<script>alert(1)</script>'). 2. Observe the response and verify the stored data.

Test Data: {"customerName": "Test Customer", "customerPhone": "1234567890", "items": [{"itemId": 1, "measurementGroups": [{"deliveryDate": "2023-12-31", "makingCharge": 100, "specialInstruction": "<script>alert(1)</script>", "measurements": []}]}]}
Expected Result: The API responds with HTTP status 200 (OK) and the order is created successfully. The special instructions field is stored and returned as plain text (not executed as script).

Title: Verify that special instructions in order items do not expose sensitive data when retrieved
Preconditions: An order exists with special instructions containing mock sensitive data (e.g., 'Customer PIN: 1234').
Steps:
1. Send a GET request to /api/orders/{orderId} to retrieve the order details. 2. Observe the response and verify the special instructions field.

Test Data: orderId = [ID of existing order]
Expected Result: The API responds with HTTP status 200 (OK) and the special instructions field is returned as-is. If the instructions contain sensitive data, this is a finding (but not a security bug in the code change itself).

Title: Verify that special instructions in order items are not logged or exposed in error messages
Preconditions: User has valid authentication token for a shop and a customer exists.
Steps:
1. Send a POST request to /api/orders with a payload containing special instructions with long or malformed content to trigger an error. 2. Observe the error response and server logs (if accessible).

Test Data: {"customerName": "Test Customer", "customerPhone": "1234567890", "items": [{"itemId": 1, "measurementGroups": [{"deliveryDate": "2023-12-31", "makingCharge": 100, "specialInstruction": "A very long string... [repeat 10,000 characters]", "measurements": []}]}]}
Expected Result: The API responds with HTTP status 400 (Bad Request) or 500 (Internal Server Error) and a generic error message (e.g., 'Invalid request' or 'An error occurred'). The error message and logs do not contain the special instructions content.
